DATA & METHODS

Behind the atlas

49,408 habitat grid cells, 56,597 habitat records. Cells can contain more than one habitat. The map displays the retained habitat footprint, with SST values attached using the corrected manuscript sampling table.

Heatwave records

GHRSST MUR v4.1: 0.01°, 2003–2025, baseline 2003–2022. OISST v2.1: 0.25°, 1982–2025, baseline 1982–2011. Heatwaves exceed the seasonally varying 90th-percentile threshold for at least five consecutive days, using the study’s no-leap calendar. Intensity is measured above the 90th-percentile threshold.

The map locations are habitat cells. Multiple habitat cells can share an SST source cell; selecting a cell shows its source coordinate and sampling distance. OISST values retain their 0.25° resolution. Zero-event years have zero days, frequency and cumulative intensity; duration and temperature intensity are missing.

Annual reconstruction

MUR annual metrics were reconstructed from the saved event catalogue using the same code as the corrected manuscript summaries. Cross-year cumulative intensity is apportioned by event days. Event frequency follows the existing pipeline, including year and no-leap calendar boundaries. All six metrics were checked against all nine habitat–ecoregion series in both products.

Climate indices

Niño-3.4, IOD, NAO, AO, EAWR, North Atlantic SST anomaly and PDO come from the manuscript’s cached NOAA archive. Annual indices are calendar-year means. Positive leads pair heatwave year y with index year y − lead. Missing early index values are excluded, without filling gaps.

Fitted variation

The selected pixel’s annual metric is fitted by ordinary least squares with an intercept, the seven annual climate indices and either year or annual mean OISST SST at the attached habitat source cell. Predictors are standardised over complete observations in the selected period. Year measures long-term change; annual SST measures local thermal covariation.

Shapley R² averages each predictor’s additional R² across all possible orders of entry into the model. Shares sum to the full model R², with correlated predictors sharing credit. These are statistical associations, rather than causal warming attribution. Leave-one-year-out R² uses the linear-model PRESS residuals; it measures held-out fit with the full selected predictor set and is separate from the manuscript’s chronological seasonal warning tests.

The paired plot independently removes a linear trend from both series when selected. Correlation is calculated from those plotted pairs. Changing the paired-plot detrending option does not change the multivariate model.

Annual mean SST

OISST daily SST was averaged within each calendar year at the 325 native SST cells attached to retained habitat cells. In the MUR view this is a separately labelled OISST covariate at the same habitat location. A time trend or annual mean SST is not a measurement of anthropogenic forcing.

Satellite imagery and habitat coverage

The satellite basemap is Esri World Imagery, with credits displayed on the map. It is a reference mosaic; imagery dates vary and do not follow the selected heatwave year. The coastline-only basemap remains available. Habitat coverage uses rendered map layers from the same study inventories (coral reefs 2021, seagrass 2021, mangroves 2010). Original GIS polygons and attributes are not redistributed.

Updated climate and seasonal probabilities

NOAA monthly feeds and dated seasonal estimates refresh weekly through GitHub Actions. Study-period indices and heatwave arrays stay unchanged. New monthly climate observations are appended from the same sources; missing months remain blank. The IOD/HadISST feed is currently delayed, so the fixed live-outlook panel uses the other six indices, with a separate matched backtest.

Forecasts use each habitat overall, each habitat within an ecoregion, or the selected SST cell. Group outcomes are mean seasonal MHW days; pixel outcomes use the source cell’s own history. High exposure exceeds the training same-season 80th percentile, with a 10-day floor. Three-month mean climate indices end two calendar months before the issue month. A ridge logistic model removes each predictor’s training-period linear trend and standardises using training values. Regularisation is chosen through earlier-season-only validation. No recent MHW observations from 2026 are assumed.

The backtest refits at every earlier-year origin, starting with 12 training seasons, with the exposure threshold and regularisation reselected from the past. Each card reports Brier skill relative to the historical-probability baseline, using evaluation years after the SST baseline was available. The full retrospective score and training dates are in the card details. These six-index estimates have not established operational alert reliability; warning levels are disabled. The eight-predictor annual pixel association model is a separate analysis.

Each pixel has its own threshold, fitted coefficients and training-only regularisation choice. Habitat points sharing an SST source cell share its forecast. The probability map uses these individual cell models. The scale selector provides habitat-wide and regional context; whole-habitat estimates use pooled exposure histories. Pixel backtests can have higher or lower skill than group models.

Point reports and contacts

“Create point report” downloads a PDF with the selected location, source sampling, all six annual histories, seasonal outlook, backtest, climate associations and author contacts. Reports are generated locally in the browser. Coral reefs, seagrass and mangroves are habitat groups; the probabilities describe heatwave exposure.
